name: Suxamethonium
status: DRAFT – pharmacology (†) is not yet checked against the package insert; doses are extracted automatically from the guideline text
dagger_note: † = general pharmacology; not in the SA guideline and not yet checked against the package insert
item_format: t=text, s=source:printed page, d=dagger, b=bold, h=heading

moa.t: Persistently depolarises the motor end plate, fastest onset, shortest duration

dosing_note: Doses are extracted automatically from the guideline text. Each heading is the nearest section title in the guideline and can be off by one section – confirm on the cited page. The pathway dose stays authoritative for its indication.

items.t: Suxamethonium, IV, 1–1.5 mg/kg. · Onset 30–60 seconds. · Duration 5 minutes.

dosing.h: Anaesthetic management of an unstable ruptured ectopic pregnancy

items.t: Suxamethonium 100 mg intravenously can be given by practitioners confident of intubation (usual dose is 1-1.5mg/kg). · The trachea should be intubated.

contraindications.t: Burns, crush injury, spinal cord injury or denervation after 24–48 hours

cautions.t: For use only by clinicians able to manage the airway

adverse_effects.t: Hyperkalaemia, bradycardia (especially children and repeat doses), fasciculations and myalgia, malignant hyperthermia, prolonged apnoea, raised intra-ocular and intragastric pressure
